issue: The verify.py generated by analyze_program.py checked manifest membership and per-file hashes but never compared the packet directory's actual entries with EXPECTED_FILES, so an unlisted file, directory or dangling symlink was ignored and the packet verified as complete.
finding: deep_disassembly.py, deep_section_analysis.py and bytecode_signatures.py gained 'packet directory entry set mismatch' in PR #3036 (commit 43506229f, research/tooling-generated-packet-census-20261031) and tests/test_generated_packet_census.py was written for them; analyze_program.py uses the same template but was omitted from both.

reproduction.fixed: python -I -B <temp>/packet/verify.py -> 'FAIL: packet directory entry set mismatch', exit 1
reproduction.variants: the same holds for an added empty directory and for a dangling symlink; the extra entry is never deleted

change.verifier: insert the sibling census check at the top of the generated main(): set(os.listdir(PACKET)) != EXPECTED_FILES | {'manifest.json'}

tests.before: tests/test_generated_packet_census.py: 3 failures (extra file, extra directory, extra symlink for analyze_program)

dependent_packets.research/tooling-analysis-output-retenti: already fails on the base revision for the same generator (its accepted-helper hashes predate base), so this change introduces no new failure there

unchanged: packet contents and generated hashes for existing entries
not_claimed: No regeneration of archived packets; the check applies to newly generated packets only.
